uncited: This family encompasses techniques that accelerate volume rendering by optimizing the efficiency of ray-grid traversal and determining optimal data structures for a given scene.
It addresses the computational bottleneck of evaluating every voxel or primitive along a ray, which is often redundant due to empty space or coarse sampling.

Unlike sibling methods that define specific traversal algorithms (e.g., DDA, Octree), this family focuses on *how* to execute traversal more efficiently (via hardware awareness or algorithmic shortcuts) and *what* resolution to use (via cost models) to minimize total rendering time.
All methods in this family build on [Ray-grid traversal](17-ray-grid-traversal.md), which advances analytically from one cell boundary to the next .
The core mechanism determines the next cell by comparing distances to upcoming boundaries on the x, y, and z axes, selecting the minimum distance to advance .
Optimization and cost models do not alter this fundamental geometric logic but instead optimize the *cost* of executing it or the *parameters* (like grid resolution) under which it runs.
The need for optimization in volume rendering arises from the high memory bandwidth and computational cost of sampling dense voxel grids.
Early methods relied on fixed-step ray marching, which was inefficient for sparse data.
The shift towards analytical traversal (DDA) provided a baseline for optimization.
Cost models, such as those by , provide theoretical bounds for grid resolution, while hardware-specific optimizations became critical with the rise of GPUs and SIMD architectures.
